newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN REFINERY KEEPS STEADY OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN REFINERY KEEPS STEADY OUTPUT.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim, which supplies the whole domestic market, plans to process 600,000 tonnes of crude this month and a total of six million tonnes this year, plant officials said on Friday.
Neftohim's executive director Nikola Karagyozov said the plant's production, which was some 630,000 tonnes last month, was steady and daily refining volumes were some 20,000 tonnes.
"I think that now we meet 100 percent of the needs of the domestic market," Karagyozov told Reuters by telephone.
He said part of the oil deliveries this month would come from Rosbulneft, a Bulgarian-Russian joint venture between Neftohim and Rosneft.
He declined to name the other suppliers.

Local media said they included China's European-based Xinohem and two local firms -- Glenkor and Litexcomers. Neftohim is negotiating for a tanker with British Bay Oil, which was the refinery's main supplier in 1992, it added.
Karagyozov said the plant had processed 5.4 million tonnes of crude in the first 10 months of the year.

Neftohim's initial plans were to raise its total output this year by 310,000 tonnes to 7.65 million tonnes. But officials said the plant was expected to refine a total of six million tonnes this year.

Foreign firms, including South Korean refineries, have sent their offers for building the refinery's catalytic reforming installation, which is crucial for the enlargement of the plant's output, officials said.

The 31-year-old plant at the Black Sea port of Bourgas is now the only oil refinery in the country after the sale of a Pleven-based refinery, Plama, earlier this year. Last November Plama suspended its production due to cash shortages.
Plama's new owner, Bulgaria's Euroenergy, said it planned to resume the refinery's output in November.
